0.long_answer: Canavan disease is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by spongiform degeneration of the brain’s white matter. The white matter is largely composed of myelin, a lipid-rich substance that insulates nerve fibers. In the central nervous system, myelin is produced and maintained by specialized glial cells known as oligodendrocytes. The degeneration observed in Canavan disease primarily affects the material produced by these cells, leading to impaired myelin synthesis and disruption of normal neural function.
